evals.name: toctou-finalizer-refunds-funded-sale
evals.prompt: Review the payment code in fixture-a (finalize.sql and handler.ts) for defects that could cause money to be lost, double-spent, or refunded incorrectly.
evals.seeded_bug: finalize.sql looks up seat_sales by payment_id BEFORE `select ... for update` and never repeats it after the lock. A concurrent duplicate delivery of an already-finalized payment wakes to the bumped version and raises STALE_QUOTE, which handler.ts refunds -- so the buyer keeps the seat AND gets their money back.
assertions: Identifies that the idempotency lookup on seat_sales runs before the FOR UPDATE lock and is never re-checked after it
Describes the concurrent-duplicate-delivery scenario that reaches STALE_QUOTE for an already-finalized payment
Connects it to the money consequence: handler.ts refunds a sale that is already funded
Rates the finding high or critical severity

evals.name: retryable-500-discards-its-own-retry
evals.prompt: Review the signed webhook handler in fixture-b for defects that could cause money to be lost or a payment event silently dropped, given its documented 200/500 retry contract.
evals.seeded_bug: The dispute branch returns 500 to request redelivery but never moves the event row off status "received". The duplicate handler answers any "received" row with 200 {duplicate, inProgress}, so the requested retry is terminally acknowledged and the chargeback is never recorded -- logged only at info level.
assertions: Identifies that the dispute-store 500 path leaves the event row on status "received"
Traces the next delivery to the "received" branch and notes it returns HTTP 200, discarding the retry
Contrasts with the processPayment catch block, which marks "error" before its 500
Rates the finding high or critical severity
